passage:
Before every test, Nora used the same yellow pencil. She believed it brought her luck.
One day, she lost it before an English test. She became so nervous that she could hardly read the first question.
Her friend gave her another pencil and whispered, "The answers are in your head, not in the pencil."
Nora took a deep breath and started writing. The test was difficult, but she finished it.
When the grades came back, she did well. Later, she found the yellow pencil under her bed, but it no longer felt magical.
She still kept it because she liked it. But she knew the real luck had been practice, calmness, and a friend's good words.
